Why I close SSH port 22 entirely (and what I use instead)

June 11, 2026 7-minute read
Linux • Software
Ssh • Security • Fwknop

Most SSH hardening guides stop at key-only authentication and fail2ban. That helps, but if your machine has a public IP, port 22 is still open to the internet.

Every automated scanner can probe the server and get a response: the SSH version string, the banner, and proof that something is listening.

The idea: port knocking, and why it is not enough on its own

The server watches for a specific sequence of connection attempts on closed ports before temporarily allowing an authenticated connection.
